schedule_contrast.interpretation: The arms do not have exactly matched teacher-turn budgets or state distributions; this is exploratory and does not show a schedule advantage.

interpretation: The frozen first-four-turn teacher block improved complete-game outcomes relative to direct on this fresh pool, with gains in both root seats. One and two early teacher turns were unresolved, but the direct first_4 versus first_1 map comparison was also unresolved. Eight early turns were not better than direct, so the benefit is not monotonic with block length. Distributed 25-percent teacher turns matched the first-four-turn win count closely. These seven descriptive contrasts share maps and baselines; their unadjusted p-values are not policy-promotion evidence, an exact macro-plan credit label, or proof that consecutive search is causally necessary.
next_decision: Do not train a neural student on this one fresh exploratory window. If testing a temporally coherent distillation target, first independently confirm the first-four-turn benefit and a direct block-versus-distributed contrast on a predeclared disjoint map window, while retaining explicit terminal/censor and both-seat gates. Otherwise investigate state-dependent teacher scheduling rather than treating block length as a monotonic hyperparameter.
